objects.description: Singleton-like utility class encapsulating image resolution (width, height) and derived pixel count. Access via Resolution::getInstance(width, height) on first use; subsequent calls likely return the same instance. Constructor is private, enforcing controlled initialization. All members are immutable once constructed. Note: actual implementation of getInstance is not shown here; thread-safety and reinitialization semantics are unknown.

Singleton-like camera intrinsics holder storing focal lengths (fx, fy) and principal point (cx, cy). Access via Intrinsics::getInstance(fx, fy, cx, cy) on first use; constructor is private and members are immutable. The getInstance implementation is not present here; initialization order, thread-safety, and whether values can be changed after first call are unspecified.

functions.name: Resolution::getInstance
functions.signature: static const Resolution& Resolution::getInstance(int width = 0, int height = 0)
functions.description: Returns a reference to the singleton Resolution instance representing image dimensions. Intended to be called first with valid width/height to initialize the singleton; subsequent calls return the same instance.
requirements: On the first call, width must be > 0 and height must be > 0 (the constructor asserts width > 0 && height > 0).
Subsequent calls likely return the already-initialized instance; behavior of passing different dimensions after initialization is unknown (implementation not shown).
The returned reference remains valid for the lifetime of the process/singleton; do not assume thread-safety (not documented).

functions.name: Intrinsics::getInstance
functions.signature: static const Intrinsics& Intrinsics::getInstance(float fx = 0, float fy = 0, float cx = 0, float cy = 0)
functions.description: Returns a reference to the singleton Intrinsics instance representing camera intrinsics (fx, fy, cx, cy). Intended to be called first with valid parameters to initialize the singleton; subsequent calls return the same instance.
requirements: On the first call, fx must be non-zero and fy must be non-zero (the constructor asserts fx != 0 && fy != 0).
cx and cy may be zero; no assertion is enforced on them.
Subsequent calls likely return the already-initialized instance; behavior of passing different parameters after initialization is unknown (implementation not shown).
The returned reference remains valid for the lifetime of the process/singleton; do not assume thread-safety (not documented).
